meta.command: npm run -s eval:form -- --pass review --provider opencode2 --model opencode-go/mimo-v2.6-flash --only c17-clean-tempting --runs 8 --timeout-min 10

findings.title: parseSettings accepts `__proto__`/`constructor`/`prototype` keys as ordinary settings
findings.detail: src/loadConfig.ts:20-24 validates only that values are strings, so a config file like '{"__proto__":"..."}' passes and the returned object carries an own `__proto__` data property (verified: JSON.parse defines it via DefineOwnProperty). There is no pollution path today (string values are required, and the `__proto__` setter ignores non-object values), and this diff has no merging consumer yet, so this is a hardening suggestion only: reject the three special keys in the validation loop so future deep-merge consumers of Settings never inherit a prototype-pollution sink.

findings.title: parseSettings rejects valid JSON that carries a UTF-8 BOM
findings.detail: Input: '\uFEFF{"a":"1"}' — a valid settings file saved with a byte-order mark (common from Windows editors) and passed as utf8 text to parseSettings (the error message shows this function is the read boundary for f.json). JSON.parse throws because U+FEFF is not legal JSON whitespace, so parseSettings throws 'cannot read settings from f.json' instead of returning {a:'1'}. RFC 8259 §8.1 permits parsers to ignore a leading BOM; strip /^\uFEFF/ (or decode BOM-aware) before JSON.parse so valid settings files load.

findings.title: pick returns the value unchecked, relying only on the type-level Settings contract
findings.detail: pick's only runtime test is Object.hasOwn; the value is then returned via a non-null assertion. Any Settings-shaped object not produced by parseSettings (a JS caller, or a future producer that relaxes validation) such as {a: 1} passes the hasOwn check, and pick({a:1},'a') returns the number 1 — the failure then surfaces much later as '1.trim is not a function' instead of at the settings boundary. Within this diff parseSettings does guarantee strings, so this is a hardening gap only.

findings.title: Some parseSettings error paths are untested
findings.detail: Tests cover '[]', 'null' and '{"a":1}', but not top-level non-object JSON primitives such as '"x"', '1' or 'true', and the 'settings in f.json must be an object' message is never asserted (only the TypeError class), nor is the empty-object happy path. A regression in that message or class would not be caught.

findings.title: JSON syntax errors and shape errors use inconsistent error classes
findings.detail: Malformed JSON throws a plain Error (line 15) while wrong-shape settings throw TypeError (lines 18 and 22), so a caller using `instanceof TypeError` to detect 'the file is malformed' cannot distinguish syntax failure from shape failure. The cause chain preserves the original SyntaxError, so this is a contract-clarity nit rather than a defect.

findings.title: Config errors use inconsistent error types between pick and parseSettings
findings.detail: parseSettings throws TypeError for malformed config (arrays, null, non-string values) but pick throws a plain Error for a missing key (line 5). A caller that classifies config problems with `err instanceof TypeError` will treat a genuine missing setting as an unexpected internal error instead of a user-facing config error, so the two failure modes of the same configuration surface get different handling paths.

findings.title: Error messages misdescribe the failure: 'read' for a parse error, 'must be an object' for arrays
findings.detail: A JSON syntax error is reported as `cannot read settings from ${source}` (line 15) even though nothing was read — only text was parsed — which sends whoever debugs the failure toward file I/O instead of JSON syntax (the original SyntaxError is only visible via `cause`). Separately, an array root yields `settings in X must be an object` (line 18), but arrays are objects in JavaScript, so the message contradicts the observed type. Both are wording issues that slow down diagnosis.

findings.title: Tests skip primitive JSON roots and inherited-property lookups in pick
findings.detail: The suite covers object/array/null/non-string-value roots and present/missing own keys, but never `parseSettings('1')`, `parseSettings('"s"')` or `parseSettings('true')` (handled correctly by the `typeof raw !== 'object'` guard, so no bug today), nor `pick(obj, 'toString')` — the inherited-property case that `Object.hasOwn` exists to reject. If the `typeof` guard or `Object.hasOwn` were later weakened to `in` or a plain truthiness check, no test would fail.

findings.title: pick returns values without verifying they are strings
findings.detail: Object.hasOwn only proves the key exists; `settings[key]!` then trusts the Settings type. A Settings object built outside parseSettings (e.g. `{ a: undefined }` from spreading partial defaults) makes pick return undefined typed as string, so downstream checks like `value === 'true'` silently take the wrong branch, whereas parseSettings rejects that same shape with 'setting a in f.json must be a string'. Re-check typeof settings[key] === 'string' (or drop the `!`) so both entry points enforce the invariant.

findings.title: JSON syntax errors are hidden from the error message
findings.detail: parseSettings replaces the SyntaxError with 'cannot read settings from f.json' and keeps the detail only in err.cause (line 15). Loggers and callers that print only err.message — the common case — report no reason or position for a malformed file, which is exactly what is needed to fix it. Append the cause message (or otherwise surface it) so the failure is diagnosable from the message alone.

findings.title: A UTF-8 BOM makes otherwise-valid config files unparseable
findings.detail: JSON.parse rejects a leading U+FEFF, so a settings file saved as UTF-8-with-BOM (common from Windows editors) containing valid JSON fails the load with 'cannot read settings from f.json' — the entire config is rejected and, with message-only logging, the real cause stays invisible. Strip a leading \uFEFF from text before parsing, or surface the cause message.

findings.title: Module named loadConfig does no loading and has no callers yet
findings.detail: The diff adds only parseSettings (pure text parsing) and pick; nothing in the diff reads a file, resolves a path, or invokes these functions outside the new test. As committed the feature is an unintegrated partial slice — fine as an incremental branch step, but no user-visible behavior ships with it.
